title.en: First case of H5 bird flu confirmed in Australia
title.zh: 澳大利亚确诊首例H5禽流感病例

summary.en: A migratory sea bird in Western Australia has tested positive for the contagious H5 variant of bird flu, marking the first detected case of this strain on the continent. Australia had previously been the only continent without a confirmed detection of the H5 bird flu strain.
summary.zh: 西澳大利亚州的一只候鸟被检测出H5型高致病性禽流感病毒呈阳性，这是该毒株首次在澳大利亚大陆被发现。此前，澳大利亚是唯一没有检测到该毒株的洲。

body.en:
A migratory sea bird tested positive for the contagious H5 variant of bird flu in Western Australia. Up until now Australia was the only continent which had not detected the strain.

Australia on Saturday confirmed its first mainland case of the deadly H5 strain of bird flu .

The disease was detected in a migratory sea bird — a brown skua — in a remote part ‌of ⁠Western Australia, Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said at a press briefing in Canberra.

The development means that the highly contagious variant of avian influenza is now present on every continent.

The bird was found near a beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park, about ​700 ‌kilometers (430 miles) from Western Australia's capital, Perth.

"Whilst disappointing, this is not unexpected, given the global spread of the H5 bird flu," Collins said.

"I can confirm there is still no evidence of any mass mortalities at this time, nor is there any evidence of infection in any poultry," she said.

The H5 strain has led to high death rates in poultry and wild birds throughout the planet.

It has also affected mammals, with detections in animals like cats, goats, alpacas and pigs.

Australia had been gearing up for the variant's arrival with stricter biosecurity at farms, testing of shore birds and vaccinations among species that were vulnerable.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said that the detection of the case was concerning, adding that his government would undertake steps to curb the spread of the disease.

"This is something that has happened through migratory birds, and has happened by definition around the world, and this is why we are preparing for this," he said.

title.en: Deadly H5 strain of bird flu has been confirmed in Australia. Here's what it means
title.zh: 澳大利亚确诊致命H5禽流感。这意味着什么？

summary.en: Australia's first case of the deadly H5N1 avian influenza has been confirmed.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚确诊了首例致命的H5N1禽流感病例。

body.en:
For years, as cases of the deadly H5 strain of bird influenza wreaked havoc among animal populations across the globe, Australia had been the sole continent to avoid it successfully — until now. The first positive case of the virus on the Australian mainland was confirmed on Saturday.

In a Canberra press conference, federal agriculture minister Julie Collins has confirmed H5 bird flu was detected in a migratory bird found in Western Australia.

A single migratory wild seabird potentially infected with the disease was found in Western Australia on June 14.

Before the suspected positive case was confirmed, Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said on Friday it would be "not unexpected".

"This will be sobering, but not unexpected given the spread globally," Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said.

The bird was a sub-Antarctic species — a brown skua bird. It was found on a remote beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park near Esperance, about 700km southeast of Perth.

WA Agriculture and Food Minister Jackie Jarvis said the bird was isolated after it was located in an unwell state on Sunday and died that night.

"I'm told it is not normal for them to be on the south coast of Western Australia," Jarvis said.

"But I am also told it's not uncommon if a bird is sick to actually be sort of blown off course, as it were."

Commonly known as bird flu, avian influenza is a contagious virus that predominantly affects bird species and can infect other animal populations, including humans.

The highly pathogenic H5N1 strain of avian influenza was discovered more than 20 years ago. Bird flu strains are classed in seriousness on a scale of pathogenicity — the capacity of the strain to cause the disease.

In birds, including poultry, seabirds and dense wild-bird colonies, H5 viruses can spread rapidly and cause severe disease, neurological defects and sudden death. Infected birds spread the virus through respiratory secretions and faeces, contaminating water, soil, feathers, carcasses and shared environments.

Australia has had previous outbreaks of avian influenza in poultry, but historically these have involved other strains, particularly H7 viruses, rather than the globally dominant H5N1 lineage.

The country’s first reported human H5N1 case in 2024 was travel-associated, in a child who likely acquired the infection overseas and later recovered.

More recently, H5 bird flu was confirmed in wildlife on Heard Island, a remote sub-Antarctic external territory of Australia. Researchers believe the strain killed thousands of elephant seal cubs. A new report found 13,000 of 17,000 baby seals on Heard Island...

title.en: US to stop funding HIV programmes in South Africa
title.zh: 美国将停止资助南非的艾滋病项目

summary.en: US officials have announced a halt to funding for HIV programs in South Africa, a country with over eight million people living with HIV, the highest number globally.
summary.zh: 美国官员宣布停止对南非艾滋病项目的资助。南非有超过八百万人感染艾滋病，是全球感染人数最多的国家。

body.en:
The US government says it will stop funding programmes in South Africa intended to tackle the spread of HIV and Aids.

More than eight million South Africans are living with HIV – the highest number of any country in the world.

The US State Department appeared to link the decision to South Africa's alleged failure to protect the white-minority Afrikaner community - an allegation the South African government has repeatedly rejected.

South Africa's health ministry responded by saying that though it had not been informed of this decision, it had "long been working on a self-reliance plan".

Until 2025, the US was supporting South Africa's efforts to deal with the virus with an estimated $400m (£300m) a year through the President's Emergency Fund for Aids Relief (Pepfar).

But since the inauguration of President Donald Trump, relations between the two countries have increasingly soured.

Shortly after he came into office, Trump issued an executive order alleging that "countless" South African policies dismantled equal opportunities and fuelled violence "against racially disfavored landowners".

This is disputed by the South African government, which says its Black Economic Empowerment policy is needed to correct economic inequality dating from the apartheid era.

The executive order also highlighted South Africa's case against Israel at the International Court of Justice and its links to Iran.

The White House said that given these "unjust and immoral practices", further aid to South Africa would not be provided.

Trump has also falsely alleged that there is a "white genocide" taking place in South Africa, which has led to the administration setting up a refugee programme for Afrikaners - descendants of western Europeans who settled in southern Africa in the 17th Century. They are now just about the only refugees being allowed into the US .

Pepfar funding, which had been providing about a fifth of South Africa's total spending on HIV programmes, got a reprieve last October with what was called a "bridge plan".

But a US State Department official has confirmed that a "phased drawdown" of Pepfar funding would now start.

This was because of "South Africa's failure to make demonstrable progress on policy requests by the administration", the official said.

The intention of the US government was to "foster self-reliance" and reduce dependency on American funding, they added, pointing out that "South Africa is a middle-income country and is more than capable of supporting its own health programs".

South Africa's health ministry has said that while Pepfar contributed to the country's HIV programme, the provision of life-saving antiretroviral drugs was funded entirely separately, with most coming from the government.

title.zh: 特朗普揭幕新空军一号，由卡塔尔航空的波音747改装

summary.en: Donald Trump unveiled a new temporary Air Force One, a converted Qatari 747, at Joint Base Andrews. The $400 million jet, named VC-25B Bridge, had previously drawn protests for exceeding limits on unsolicited gifts.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在安德鲁斯联合基地揭幕了一架新的临时空军一号，这是一架由卡塔尔航空的波音747改装而成的飞机。这架名为VC-25B Bridge的4亿美元喷气式飞机此前因超出未经请求的礼物限额而引发抗议。

body.en: New craft, called VC-25B Bridge, had provoked protest since $400m jet wildly exceeds limit on unsolicited gifts Donald Trump unveiled the new, temporary Air Force One at a hangar at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland on Friday, a day after White House officials bid farewell to one of two Boeing 747s used to transport presidents for more than 30 years. The new jet, designated VC-25B and decked out in a punchy red, white, dark blue and gold livery, was gifted to Trump by the Gulf emirate of Qatar, provoking howls of political protest since the $400m jet wildly exceeds the limit on unsolicited gifts of $50 in value in a single calendar year from the same source. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这架名为 VC-25B Bridge 的新飞机引发了抗议，因为价值 4 亿美元的喷气式飞机严重超出了主动赠送礼物的限制。周五，唐纳德·特朗普在马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地的机库推出了新的临时空军一号，一天前，白宫官员告别了 30 多年来用来运送总统的两架波音 747 中的一架。这架新飞机被命名为 VC-25B，采用醒目的红色、白色、深蓝色和金色涂装，是海湾酋长国卡塔尔赠送给特朗普的礼物，引发了政治抗议，因为这架价值 4 亿美元的飞机远远超出了同一来源在一个日历年内主动赠送礼物价值 50 美元的限制。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The unveiling of a costly new presidential aircraft, especially one that sparked protests over its value and origin, highlights the tension between public service and material display. It reminds us to consider where our ultimate loyalties lie, as Yahweh teaches that we cannot truly serve both Him and worldly wealth.
reflection.zh: 一架耗资巨大的新总统专机揭幕，尤其是在其价值和来源引发抗议的情况下，凸显了公共服务与物质展示之间的张力。这提醒我们思考我们的最终忠诚所在，因为雅伟教导我们不能真正地同时侍奉祂和世俗的财富。

verse.textEn: No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and Mammon.
verse.textZh: 一个人不能事奉两个主……你们不能又事奉神，又事奉玛门。

title.en: Train driver dies and 89 people injured after two trains collide near Bedford
title.zh: 贝德福德附近两列火车相撞，据报有人员受伤

summary.en: Two trains collided near Bedford, causing injuries and leading to the closure of railway lines between Luton and Bedford. Emergency services, including police, are currently at the scene responding to the incident.
summary.zh: 两列火车在贝德福德附近相撞，造成人员受伤，并导致卢顿和贝德福德之间的铁路线关闭。包括警察在内的紧急服务人员正在现场处理事故。

body.en: Eleven people suffer ‘very serious’ injuries, with emergency services still at the scene into the night A train driver has died and 89 people have been injured after two trains collided in the Bedford area, with emergency services working into the night. Of those injured, 11 people suffered “very serious” injuries and 22 were seriously injured, East of England ambulance service said, while a further 56 people had minor injuries and were treated at the scene or taken to hospital. Continue reading...
body.zh: 当局表示，两列火车在贝德福德地区相撞，警察和其他紧急服务人员在现场。 据泰晤士联线称，此次碰撞造成人员受伤，并导致晚间通勤严重延误，卢顿和贝德福德之间的线路已关闭。 下午 5 点 30 分左右，东米德兰铁路公司 (East Midlands Railway) 在 X 上发布消息称，“由于紧急服务处理事故”，伦敦圣潘克拉斯和莱斯特之间的火车无法运行。 英国交通警察局表示，其警员正在对这起碰撞事件做出反应，贝德福德郡警方和贝德福德郡消防救援部门也在采取行动。 受伤乘客的亲友已被要求不要前往现场。 铁路、海事和运输工会发言人表示，他们对火车相撞以及“车上工作人员和乘客严重受伤”的报道深感担忧。 火车运营商补充说，今天剩余时间里，东米德兰铁路往返伦敦圣潘克拉斯的服务已暂停。 交通大臣海蒂·亚历山大 (Heidi Alexander) 在 X 上写道：“听到有关两列东米德兰铁路客运列车相撞的报道，我深感担忧。 “我感谢在现场照顾受影响人员的紧急服务人员。 “我们正在与铁路行业和当地合作伙伴迅速合作，为乘客提供支持。” 英格兰东部救护车服务部门表示，一架空中救护车和危险区域反应小组正在对贝德福德以南的“重大事件”做出反应。 社交媒体上发布的视频显示，一辆受损的紫色卢顿机场快线列车和乘客站在铁轨上。 所涉南行列车前车厢的乘客皮特·纳普博士在 Bluesky 上发帖称：“从贝德福德向南行驶的列车于 17 点 12 分坠毁。列车前部正常，第三节车厢脱轨。 “我对流血的腿和背部的撞击没什么问题。其他的都不好。突然发生碰撞，没有减速或按喇叭。没有警告。 铁路事故调查部门表示，一组检查人员正在埃尔斯托附近的碰撞现场开始收集证据。 贝德福德和肯普斯顿议员穆罕默德·亚辛 (Mohammad Yasin) 表示，他对此事感到“非常遗憾”，并将“很快”分享更多信息。 其中一辆涉及的列车是去年投入运营的新东米德兰铁路Aurora。 Network Rail 发言人表示：“目前卢顿和贝德福德之间没有泰晤士联线服务。如果您计划在该地区旅行，强烈建议您推迟行程。” “卢顿和伦敦之间的服务严重中断。我们建议客户寻求其他旅行安排。”

reflection.en: In the wake of an unexpected collision causing injuries and disruption, our thoughts turn to those affected and the emergency responders. Yahweh is a constant refuge and strength, a present help in times of trouble, offering solace and support when life's unforeseen challenges arise.
reflection.zh: 在这次意外的火车相撞事故造成人员受伤和交通中断之后，我们的心转向受影响的人和紧急救援人员。雅伟是我们随时可得的避难所和力量，在患难中提供安慰和支持，尤其当生活中出现不可预见的挑战时。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Israel and Hezbollah agree to a ceasefire as US-Iran deal under strain
title.zh: 以色列和真主党同意停火，美伊协议面临压力

summary.en: Israel and Hezbollah have reached a ceasefire agreement following a recent escalation of violence. The flare-up resulted in 47 deaths in Lebanon and four Israeli soldiers killed, occurring amidst ongoing tensions regarding the US-Iran deal.
summary.zh: 以色列和真主党在近期暴力升级后达成停火协议。此次冲突导致黎巴嫩47人死亡，以及4名以色列士兵阵亡，事件发生在美国与伊朗协议持续紧张的背景下。

body.en:
Israel and Hezbollah agreed a ceasefire on Friday, a US official said, after deadly exchanges between the two sides in Lebanon once again put a deal to end the Middle East war under strain, less than two days after it was signed.

Lebanese authorities reported 47 people were killed in Israeli airstrikes and Israel announced the deaths of four of its soldiers, the highest combined casualty count since the US and Iran struck their deal.

Talks that were scheduled to take place between the US and Iran in Switzerland to build on the deal and work towards a lasting settlement were postponed , with no new date announced, but US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun held a call.

The Lebanese presidency said Aoun thanked Rubio for US support but stressed "the need for Israeli attacks on Lebanese territory to cease through the achievement of a comprehensive ceasefire".

Rubio, according to the US state department, insisted on the importance of Lebanon carrying through on its efforts to disarm the Hezbollah armed group, which is fighting Israel in the south of the country.

"They discussed the next round of negotiations, scheduled for June 23 to 25 in Washington, where the two sovereign governments will make progress toward a lasting peace," a spokesman said. "Secretary Rubio reiterated the need to disarm Hezbollah and to re-establish control over all Lebanese territory."

Israel's ambassador to the United States, Yechiel Leiter, insisted in a social media post that Israel was committed to an immediate ceasefire in Lebanon, but only "if Hezbollah honours the agreement and ceases its hostilities".

The deal signed this week by US President Donald Trump and his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian aims to end a war that began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes that killed supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The agreement was also meant to halt the fighting in Lebanon, which Iran has always insisted should be covered under any accord, turning Israel's ongoing campaign there into a source of frustration for Washington.

Israel's military said Friday that it had struck more than 80 Hezbollah targets in Lebanon and killed dozens of members of the Iran-backed group.

But a US official told the Agence France-Presse news agency that a truce between Israel and Hezbollah, beginning immediately, had been brokered by US and Qatari mediators following talks with Israel and Iran. A Gulf diplomat confirmed the ceasefire.

Even after the truce was announced, Lebanese state media reported an Israeli airstrike on the country's south in the Jezzine region.

Yahweh blesses those who actively work to end conflict and bring reconciliation, reflecting His own desire for peace among humanity. title.en: Zelensky stripped of highest Polish honour over WW2 name of army unit
title.zh: 泽连斯基因二战时期军队单位名称被剥夺波兰最高荣誉

summary.en: Poland has revoked the highest honour previously awarded to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, citing the World War II-era name of a Ukrainian army unit. Ukraine has condemned the decision, describing it as a "strategic mistake" and "disrespectful."
summary.zh: 波兰已撤销此前授予乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的最高荣誉，理由是乌克兰一支军队单位使用了二战时期的名称。乌克兰谴责这一举动是“战略性错误”且“不尊重”。

body.en:
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky has been stripped of Poland's highest state honour, the Order of the White Eagle, over Kyiv's decision to name a military unit after controversial World War Two fighters.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki branded Ukraine's decision late last month to name the unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) "outrageous", "incomprehensible" and "deeply disappointing".

Nawrocki stressed the diplomatic row would not impact Poland's support for Ukraine against Russia.

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha denounced Warsaw's move, calling it a "strategic mistake" and "disrespectful".

Many in Ukraine regard the UPA, which existed in the 1940s and 1950s, as heroes who fought for Ukrainian independence against the Soviet Red Army as well as Nazi Germany and Polish authorities. So for Ukrainians the title "Heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army" is a major honour.

Poland, however, accuses the UPA of carrying out a genocide of ethnic Poles in Volhynia (now Volyn in Ukraine) in 1943-45.

"For the overwhelming majority of Polish society, the UPA remains, above all, a formation responsible for the brutal crimes committed against citizens of the Republic of Poland during World War II," Nawrocki said in a video released on the president's official website.

"That is why the Ukrainian authorities' decision to glorify the UPA is not only outrageous, it is also incomprehensible and deeply disappointing," he said.

"It hurts not only our historical memory. It also undermines the trust built up over the years and in recent months," he added.

The Polish president pointed to the hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian refugees welcomed into the country following the launch of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

"Poles opened their borders, their homes, and their hearts to millions of Ukrainians," he said.

He went on to say: "Ukraine's path toward European structures also requires a willingness to honestly confront the difficult chapters of its own history.

"A united Europe was built on the rejection of totalitarianism and the cult of violence. These principles must apply to everyone. For those who do not understand this, there can be no place in the European Union, and Poland will certainly not allow it."

Ukraine has ambitions to become an EU member state and attended the first phase of membership negotiations this week in Luxembourg.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has attempted to dampen growing diplomatic tensions between Kyiv and Warsaw.

Taking to social media on Friday, the former president of the European Council said the feud "delights" Russia's Vladimir Putin and called on Zelensky and Nawrocki to "calm emotions, not to stoke tensions".

title.en: Israel's political future may come down to this one showdown
title.zh: 以色列的政治未来可能取决于这场对决

summary.en: Israel is facing a crucial election that will determine its political future, with voters choosing between the incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu's faction and those seeking to replace him.
summary.zh: 以色列正面临一场决定其政治未来的关键选举，选民将在本雅明·内塔尼亚胡的阵营和寻求取代他的人之间做出选择。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

There's an enormous amount at stake for Israelis — and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — as the country prepares to head to the polls later this year.

Things look very different in Israel since its last elections. The country suffered the deadliest attack in its history on 7 October 2023, precipitating a prolonged conflict in Gaza that has been followed by a wider regional escalation involving Iran and Lebanon.

Surveys indicate public support of Israel has deteriorated significantly in the United States and among other Western allies since the start of the Hamas-Israel war .

And Netanyahu, embroiled in a long-running corruption trial domestically, is also the subject of an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant over alleged war crimes in Gaza, allegations Israel rejects.

Polls suggest Netanyahu, who has served nearly 19 non-consecutive years in office since he was first elected in 1996, remains a dominant political figure, but enters the election period vulnerable.

While his Likud party generally leads in the polls, it can't form a government alone, and an alliance of new and existing opposition parties could end up with more seats than his broader right-wing coalition.

His frayed coalition government, composed of five parties and considered the most right-wing in Israel's history, moved last month to dissolve parliament, setting the stage to move the election up from its original date of 27 October.

Some have billed it as one of the most consequential votes in Israel's history, and a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership following the October 7 attacks.

The election is set to be a defining test of Netanyahu's leadership and of how more than two years of conflict have reshaped Israel’s political landscape.

Netanyahu's coalition has been at odds over a controversial issue that has long divided Israeli society: the exemption of some ultra-Orthodox Jews from military conscription.

title.en: Italy's Meloni says Trump 'made up' story that she 'begged' him for photo at G7
title.zh: 意大利总理梅洛尼称特朗普“编造”了她在G7峰会“恳求”合影的故事

summary.en: Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has publicly refuted former U.S. President Donald Trump's claim that she "begged" him for a photo at the G7 summit. This public disagreement highlights a strain in their relationship, which reportedly began after Trump's decision to engage in conflict with Iran.
summary.zh: 意大利总理乔治娅·梅洛尼公开驳斥了美国前总统唐纳德·特朗普关于她在七国集团峰会上“恳求”与他合影的说法。这次高度公开的争执表明，自特朗普决定与伊朗开战以来，他们之间早先的密切关系已经出现裂痕。

body.en:
Italy's prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, has said she is astonished after President Donald Trump told Italian TV she had "begged" him for a picture with her, in comments that have provoked an open row between the two leaders.

Meloni said Trump's comments were entirely "made-up", and Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani has cancelled a trip to the US early next week.

The highly public exchange is an indication of how far their earlier close ties have frayed in the months since Trump's decision to go to war with Iran.

Trump and Meloni were seen in close conversation at the G7 summit at Evian-les-Bains in eastern France this week, and the Italian leader later told reporters their relationship was unchanged and there had been "no recriminations".

However, Trump has since given a phone interview with Italy's La7 TV channel in which he alleged: "She begged me to take a photo with her; I felt sorry for her."

The two leaders were filmed several times at Evian, including while they appeared engrossed in conversation on a small sofa, with Meloni smiling as they talked.

"She's probably happy I spoke to her," he said. La7 did not produce Trump's original words in English, but voiced them over in Italian.

Meloni reacted in total disbelief, saying she was "frankly stunned", in a brief address to her seven million followers on Instagram.

"I don't know why the US president behaves this way towards allies," she said, adding it was not the first time it had happened.

"I can only say it is regrettable he does not show the same determination towards the enemies of the West and towards the enemies of the US - [enemies] whose leaders he instead appears to be far more accommodating with."

Meloni's evident shock at Trump's outburst comes after a series of incidents that have weakened what had begun as a close political relationship.

Elected in 2022, Meloni was the sole European leader to attend Trump's inauguration in January 2025 and was widely seen by her EU colleagues as a potential bridge-builder with the US president.

But Meloni has been outspoken in her opposition to the US war with Iran and in April Trump hit back with a phone interview with Italian daily Corriere della Sera in which he said, "I thought she had courage, but I was wrong".

When Trump accused Pope Leo XIV of being "weak on crime and terrible on foreign policy", Meloni said his remarks were unacceptable.

Responding to Trump's latest interview, Italy's President Sergio Mattarella immediately phoned Meloni to offer his support, and figures from across the political spectrum in Italy sprang to her defence.

No-one had the right to speak to an Italian prime minister in such an arrogant tone, said Filippo Sensi, a senator on the left from the opposition Democratic Party.

Just as a small spark can set a large forest ablaze, careless or false statements can fray even strong alliances. This reminds us of the profound impact our words carry, especially in public discourse.

title.en: Israel and Hezbollah agree ceasefire, US says, as more Lebanon strikes reported
title.zh: 美国称以色列和真主党同意停火，黎巴嫩更多袭击被报道

summary.en: Israel and Hezbollah have agreed to a ceasefire, according to the US, following concerns that ongoing clashes could jeopardize a broader deal to end the war between the US and Iran. More strikes in Lebanon were reported as the agreement was announced.

body.en:
Israel and Hezbollah have agreed a ceasefire, a US official says, following intense Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon that killed 47 people.

The latest agreement followed concerns that continued clashes, which also saw Hezbollah kill four Israeli soldiers in Lebanon, would undermine the deal to end the war between the US and Iran.

The Israeli military confirmed that a ceasefire was in effect, but later a spokesman said its forces would "continue to remove immediate threats".

Hezbollah is yet to confirm the ceasefire but its secretary general, Sheikh Naim Qassem, said: "The project to eliminate Hezbollah has failed."

Rescue officials in the city of Nabatieh told the BBC there had been at least 12 air strikes since the ceasefire began at 16:00 local time (13:00 GMT).

The deadly escalation is another sign that Donald Trump is not necessarily in control of the fate of his deal with Iran.

The memorandum of understanding declared a ceasefire in Lebanon as well as between the US and Iran. But that has not been the reality on the ground, which has led Tehran to accuse Trump of failing to rein in Israel.

Trump himself has given fuel to this argument in an unprecedented set of accusations against his ally, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, suggesting he has been senselessly killing civilians in his fight against Hezbollah.

While the White House insists a ceasefire is in place, Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir responded to the deaths of Israeli soldiers by saying "Lebanon must burn... For every tear shed by an Israeli mother, 1,000 Lebanese mothers must weep".

In response, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused Israel of wanting "permanent war" and insisted that any breach of the commitments set out in the memorandum of understanding "will be attributed to the US".

Trump's deal relies on each side reining in hardliners and showing restraint - and there are few signs of that.

Netanyahu has been under domestic pressure to continue military operations against Hezbollah, while the Iran-backed group has said it would continue its attacks as long as Israel's invasion of southern Lebanon persists.

Following the latest ceasefire announcement, Israeli military spokesperson Effie Defrin said Israel would "continue to remove immediate threats, respond to Hezbollah's violations, and do whatever is necessary to protect our civilians".

Hezbollah's secretary general, Sheikh Naim Qassem, on Friday declared: "The project to eliminate Hezbollah has failed, and the Israelis will withdraw from every last inch of our land."

title.zh: 律师称在叙利亚被拘留的德国记者已回国

summary.en: Eva Maria Michelmann, a German journalist who disappeared in Syria in January during clashes between government forces and Kurdish fighters, has safely returned home, her lawyer confirmed. The German government had previously stated its efforts to secure her release.
summary.zh: 德国记者伊娃·玛丽亚·米歇尔曼已安全回国，其律师证实了这一消息。她于一月份在叙利亚失踪，当时政府军正在向叙利亚东北部的库尔德武装推进。德国政府上周曾表示正在努力让她回家。

body.zh: 一月份，当政府军向东北部的库尔德武装进攻时，伊娃·玛丽亚·米歇尔曼 (Eva Maria Michelmann) 在叙利亚失踪。德国政府上周表示正在努力让她回家。 德国记者伊娃·玛丽亚·米歇尔曼 (Eva Maria Michelmann) 今年年初在叙利亚报道十多年内战遗留问题时失踪，她的律师称，她已于周五返回德国。 她的律师罗兰·梅斯特告诉法新社：“可以证实，伊娃·M·米歇尔曼今天上午被释放，并于今天下午返回德国。”他也向其他媒体发表了类似评论。 她的兄弟安东尼斯·米歇尔曼后来告诉德国德新社，当她经约旦返回德国时，“我们去接她”。 他说她已被单独监禁很长时间，但没有提供更多细节。 米歇尔曼今年一月在叙利亚政府军对东北部库尔德武装的进攻中失踪。她的同事土耳其库尔德记者艾哈迈德·波拉德同时失踪。 据保护记者委员会（CPJ）称，他们都曾在伊斯坦布尔的社会主义埃特金通讯社（ETHA）和 Ozgur 电视频道工作。 德国外交部上周表示，正在高层努力确保米歇尔曼获释。 目前尚不清楚这位来自西部城市科隆的记者为何被拘留，也不清楚她是否被指控犯有任何罪行。 西方广泛欢迎由前伊斯兰激进组织领导人艾哈迈德·沙拉领导的叙利亚新政府，他承诺在大马士革掌权后将翻开新的、包容性的一页。 但包括叙利亚库尔德人在内的宗教和少数民族群体对 2024 年 12 月推翻长期独裁者巴沙尔·阿萨德的新逊尼派政权表示担忧。 除了与库尔德武装的军事冲突以及针对阿拉维派和德鲁兹派的暴力报道之外，大马士革限制酒类销售等更平常的变化也引发了批评和抗议。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间将我们选为 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.en: The safe return of a journalist from a dangerous conflict zone brings immense relief, reminding us of the profound anxiety that accompanies such disappearances. This news echoes the truth that while weeping may endure for a night of uncertainty and fear, joy often arrives with the morning of deliverance. Yahweh's faithfulness can turn seasons of distress...
reflection.zh: 一名记者从危险冲突区安全归来，带来了巨大的宽慰，也提醒我们此类失踪事件所伴随的深切焦虑。这则新闻呼应了一个真理：虽然不确定和恐惧的夜晚可能伴随着哭泣，但喜乐常常随着得蒙拯救的清晨而到来。雅伟的信实能将困境的季节转变为感恩欢庆的时刻。

verse.textEn: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.
verse.textZh: 一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。

title.en: Lebanon: Is US-Iran peace deal a 'victory' for Hezbollah?
title.zh: 黎巴嫩：美伊和平协议是真主党的“胜利”吗？

summary.en: Lebanon's Hezbollah group has claimed that the US-Iran peace deal is a "great victory." The group, which is opposed to Israel, has certainly been bolstered by the deal. But what have they really won?
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩真主党声称，美伊和平协议是其“巨大胜利”。这个反对以色列的组织无疑因该协议而受到鼓舞。但他们真正赢得了什么？

body.en:
Lebanon's Hezbollah group has claimed that the US-Iran peace deal is a "great victory." The group, which is opposed to Israel, has certainly been bolstered by the deal. But what have they really won?

"A great victory" and a "pivotal point for Lebanon" — that was how Naim Kassem, the leader of Lebanese group Hezbollah , described on Wednesday the memorandum of understanding that stopped fighting between Iran and the US  this week.

Kassem also thanked the Iranians for "linking the Lebanese arena" to the deal and "forcing Israel to stop its aggression."

Hezbollah was founded in 1982 with support from Iran, and one of its primary aims then was to end Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon. It has both a military and political wing and the support of much of Lebanon's Shiite Muslim community. Today it plays a major part in Lebanese society and politics, has often been described as a "state within a state," and remains opposed to Israel. Since Kassem's comments, fighting has continued in southern Lebanon, with Hezbollah targeting Israeli soldiers and Israel continuing to destroy southern villages and use bombs and drones. Sixty days of talks between the US and Iran, during which details would be hammered out, were due to start in Switzerland on Friday but were postponed in the morning because of Iran's opposition to the fighting in Lebanon.

Yet, despite it's troubled start, analysts say that the deal  on the table favors Hezbollah's allies in Tehran. 

"This memorandum of understanding virtually gives Iran everything it wanted and Trump everything he had [before attacking Iran, together with Israel, in February]," says James M. Dorsey, an expert on the region at Singapore's Rajaratnam School of International Studies. "And certainly, at least initially, it looks like a victory for Hezbollah."

The first paragraph of the memorandum states that the US, Iran and allies will declare an "immediate and permanent" termination of military operations on "all fronts," including Lebanon.

The deal, signed by the US, Iran and mediator Pakistan on Wednesday, also says that both will ensure "the territorial integrity and sovereignty" of Lebanon .

Israel currently occupies around 600 square kilometers in southern Lebanon and calls this a necessary "security buffer zone" needed to protect citizens in northern Israel from Hezbollah rockets. Critics of Israel say it is an invasion and occupation.

"The Iranians, for all practical purposes, said this means two things," Dorsey explained. "No more military action and an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon. body.zh: 黎巴嫩真主党声称美伊和平协议是“伟大的胜利”。这个反对以色列的组织无疑得到了该协议的支持。但他们真正赢得了什么？ “伟大的胜利”和“黎巴嫩的转折点”——周三，黎巴嫩真主党领导人纳伊姆·卡西姆这样形容伊朗和美国本周停止战斗的谅解备忘录。 卡西姆还感谢伊朗人“将黎巴嫩舞台与该协议联系起来”并“迫使以色列停止侵略”。 真主党于 1982 年在伊朗的支持下成立，当时的主要目标之一是结束以色列对黎巴嫩南部的占领。 它拥有军事和政治部门，并得到黎巴嫩什叶派穆斯林社区的支持。 如今，它在黎巴嫩社会和政治中发挥着重要作用，经常被描述为“国中之国”，并且仍然反对以色列。自卡西姆发表评论以来，黎巴嫩南部的战斗仍在继续，真主党以以色列士兵为目标，以色列继续摧毁南部村庄并使用炸弹和无人机。 美国和伊朗之间为期六十天的谈判原定于周五在瑞士开始，期间将敲定细节，但由于伊朗反对黎巴嫩战斗而于上午推迟。 然而，尽管开局不利，但分析人士表示，摆在桌面上的协议有利于真主党在德黑兰的盟友。 “这份谅解备忘录实际上为伊朗提供了它想要的一切，也为特朗普提供了他所拥有的一切（在二月份与以色列一起攻击伊朗之前），”新加坡拉惹勒南国际研究学院的该地区专家詹姆斯·M·多尔西（James M. Dorsey）表示。 “当然，至少在最初，这看起来像是真主党的胜利。” 备忘录第一段指出，美国、伊朗及其盟国将宣布“立即且永久”终止在包括黎巴嫩在内的“所有战线”的军事行动。 该协议由美国、伊朗和调解巴基斯坦周三签署，协议还表示，双方将确保黎巴嫩的“领土完整和主权”。 以色列目前占据黎巴嫩南部约600平方公里的土地，并称其为保护以色列北部公民免受真主党火箭弹袭击所需的必要“安全缓冲区”。以色列的批评者称这是入侵和占领。 “出于所有实际目的，伊朗人说这意味着两件事，”多尔西解释道。 “不再采取军事行动，以色列也从黎巴嫩撤军。因此，伊朗立场的试金石将是以色列是否被迫遵守这些条件，以及特朗普是否对以色列说，‘你......

reflection.en: In the complex landscape of international relations, groups often claim political victories, yet true peace and lasting change often involve struggles beyond mere human negotiation. This verse reminds us that underlying many conflicts are deeper spiritual forces, urging us to look beyond surface-level gains to understand what is truly at stake.
reflection.zh: 在复杂的国际关系中，各方常宣称政治上的胜利，然而真正的和平与持久的改变，往往涉及超越单纯人类谈判的争战。这节经文提醒我们，许多冲突的背后有更深层的属灵力量，敦促我们超越表面的得失，去理解真正重要的究竟是什么。

verse.textEn: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.
verse.textZh: 因我们并不是与属血气的争战，乃是与那些执政的、掌权的、管辖这幽暗世界的，以及天空属灵气的恶魔争战。

title.en: Guinea-Bissau: Opposition leader house arrest raises stakes
title.zh: 几内亚比绍：反对党领袖软禁增加赌注

summary.en: Opposition leader Domingos Simoes Pereira remains under house arrest months after the Guinea-Bissau coup, deepening a political crisis and raising tensions with international partners.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Opposition leader Domingos Simoes Pereira remains under house arrest months after the Guinea-Bissau coup, deepening a political crisis and raising tensions with international partners.

Nearly seven months after last year's military coup in Guinea-Bissau , the continued house arrest of opposition figure Domingos Simoes Pereira, leader of the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde (PAIGC), has developed into an international issue.

A Guinea‑Bissau military court earlier this month ordered Pereira to remain under house arrest after fresh questioning over allegations he plotted a coup against the military government, AFP reported, citing his lawyer.

While Portugal and other Portuguese-speaking states have called for his release, the military leadership in the West African nation's capital, Bissau, has dismissed the criticism as interference in national sovereignty.

On November 26, 2025, three days after the presidential election, Guinea-Bissau was waiting for the official announcement of the results by the National Electoral Commission, as most of the votes had already been counted.

At 12:40 p.m. local time,  gunfire and panicked screams erupted around the presidential palace and the National Electoral Commission building. Two hours later, a statement aired on state broadcaster TGB announcing an army takeover .

The electoral commission said on December 2 it could not complete the election process after armed men seized ballots and vote tallies from its offices and destroyed servers storing the results, reported Reuters.

A National Transitional Council took over governance and, under international pressure, announced new presidential and legislative elections for December 6.

Among the first people arrested was Pereira, one of the country's most prominent politicians.

"This regime knows that it lacks legitimacy; it was not elected by the people," Pereira said shortly before his arrest.

"Its power rests solely on force. We refuse to accept that," he told DW. "We demand that the political process in our country proceed in accordance with the constitution."

Pereira was released into house arrest in January after being accused of involvement in at least two attempted coups in 2023 and 2025.

Pereira's lawyer, Roberto Indeque, said that his client has not been formally provided with any legal justification for his detention.

"Domingos Simoes Pereira has been questioned twice before a military court since his arrest, and those hearings made it clear that he had absolutely no involvement in preparing a coup," Indeque said.

body.zh: 几内亚比绍政变几个月后，反对党领袖多明戈斯·西莫斯·佩雷拉仍被软禁，加剧了政治危机并加剧了与国际伙伴的紧张关系。 去年几内亚比绍发生军事政变近七个月后，几内亚和佛得角非洲独立党（PAIGC）领导人、反对派人物多明戈斯·西蒙斯·佩雷拉（Domingos Simoes Pereira）持续被软禁，已发展成为一个国际问题。 据法新社援引佩雷拉律师的消息报道，几内亚比绍军事法庭本月早些时候下令继续软禁佩雷拉，因为他被指控密谋反对军政府的政变。 尽管葡萄牙和其他葡语国家呼吁释放他，但西非国家首都比绍的军方领导层却驳回了这些批评，认为这是对国家主权的干涉。 2025年11月26日，总统选举三天后，几内亚比绍正在等待国家选举委员会正式公布结果，因为大部分选票已经清点完毕。 中午 12:40当地时间，总统府和国家选举委员会大楼周围爆发枪声和惊慌的尖叫声。两小时后，国家广播公司 TGB 发表声明，宣布军队接管。 据路透社报道，选举委员会 12 月 2 日表示，武装人员从其办公室夺取了选票和计票结果，并摧毁了存储结果的服务器，因此无法完成选举程序。 全国过渡委员会接管了治理权，并在国际压力下宣布将于 12 月 6 日举行新的总统和立法选举。 佩雷拉是第一批被捕的人之一，他是该国最著名的政治家之一。 “这个政权知道它缺乏合法性；它不是由人民选举产生的，”佩雷拉在被捕前不久说道。 “它的力量完全依赖于武力。我们拒绝接受这一点，”他告诉德国之声。 “我们要求我国的政治进程按照宪法进行。” 佩雷拉被指控参与 2023 年和 2025 年至少两次未遂政变，并于 1 月被释放并软禁。 佩雷拉的律师罗伯托·因德克表示，他的当事人尚未被正式提供任何拘留他的法律理由。 因德克说：“多明戈斯·西蒙斯·佩雷拉自被捕以来已在军事法庭接受过两次讯问，这些听证会明确表明他绝对没有参与准备政变。” 他补充说，检察官没有提出任何审前拘留的请求。 “但他仍然被拘留，即使是在他自己的家里，”他说。 “拘留就是拘留；从法律上讲，......

title.en: The collapse of 'world order' as an opportunity for Asia?
title.zh: “世界秩序”的崩溃对亚洲而言是机遇吗？

summary.en: In Europe, changes to international norms and institutional systems are often interpreted as a loss. However, these changes may also mark the beginning of a new, more inclusive order, particularly as some in Asia view them as an opportunity.
summary.zh: 在欧洲，国际规范和制度体系数十年的变化常被解读为一种损失。然而，这些变化也可能标志着一个更具包容性的新秩序的开始，尤其是在亚洲，有时被视为机遇。

body.en:
In Europe — unlike in Asia — changes to decades of international norms and institutional systems are often interpreted as a loss. However, these changes may also mark the beginning of a new, more inclusive order.

Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine on the European Union's eastern flank, the United States' disregard and contempt for the international order under President Donald Trump, and the allegations that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza have shocked many Europeans .

The world order that took shape after World War II appears to have come to an end. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated at the Munich Security Conference in February 2026: "This order, as imperfect as it was even in its best days, no longer exists in that form." 

However, in Asia, political observers are often surprised at the consternation of European leaders. During the Shangri-La Dialogue, an annual Asian security conference held in Singapore, former Singaporean diplomat Bilahari Kausikan told DW that "Europe thought the jungle had been tamed for good. And then it got a shock."

"Competition and conflict are fundamental characteristics of international relations. These enduring, harsh truths were obscured for a brief period — perhaps about 20 years from the fall of the Berlin Wall to the outbreak of the global financial crisis. This was an extraordinary phase in world history," he added.

Marc Saxer, Asia-Pacific head of Germany's Friedrich-Ebert-Foundation, told DW that European and Asian worldviews are shaped by different historical experiences. Under the protective umbrella of United States , Europe was able to dream of a liberal world order. For Asia, that was unthinkable.

Saxer considers efforts to maintain a liberal world order to have failed, and he believes that "a return by the US to the role it played until the 2010s is impossible for structural reasons."

The political analyst said the unipolar era is definitely over, as the US has overextended itself strategically with conflict zones in Europe, the Middle East and the Asia-Pacific.

Thomas Kleine-Brockhoff, director of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), told DW that the US under Trump is now attempting to "establish a hegemonic world of great powers, a kind of global directorate along with Russia and China," amounting to spheres of influence controlled by great powers.

As a result, international law and multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are being undermined by the United States, China and Russia (each for its own reasons and with its own intentions).

According to Saxer, who has published a book under the same title, the result is a "wolf world," meaning a world "in which the law of the strongest triumphs over the strength of the law."

body.zh: 在欧洲，与亚洲不同，几十年来国际规范和制度体系的变化常常被解读为一种损失。然而，这些变化也可能标志着一个更具包容性的新秩序的开始。 俄罗斯在欧盟东翼发动对乌克兰的侵略战争、美国对唐纳德·特朗普总统领导下的国际秩序的无视和蔑视，以及以色列在中东冲突中违反人道主义法的指控，令许多欧洲人感到震惊。 第二次世界大战后形成的世界秩序似乎已经结束。德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨 (Friedrich Merz) 在 2026 年 2 月的慕尼黑安全会议上表示：“这一秩序即使在最好的时候也是不完美的，但现在已经不复存在了。” 然而，在亚洲，政治观察家常常对一些欧洲人的惊愕感到惊讶。在新加坡举行的一年一度的亚洲安全会议香格里拉对话期间，新加坡前外交官比拉哈里·考斯坎 (Bilahari Kausikan) 告诉德国之声：“欧洲原以为丛林已经被永久驯服了。但随后他们感到震惊。” “竞争和冲突是国际关系的基本特征。从柏林墙倒塌到全球金融危机爆发，这些持久而严酷的事实在一段时间内被掩盖了——大约20年。这是世界历史上一个非同寻常的阶段，”他补充道。 德国弗里德里希·艾伯特基金会亚太区负责人马克·萨克瑟向德国之声表示，欧洲和亚洲的世界观是由不同的历史经历塑造的。在美国的保护伞下，欧洲得以梦想建立自由的世界秩序。对于亚洲来说，这是不可想象的。 Saxer 认为维持自由世界秩序的努力已经失败，他认为“由于结构性原因，美国不可能恢复 2010 年代之前所扮演的角色”。 这位政治分析人士表示，单极时代肯定已经结束，因为美国在欧洲、中东和亚太地区冲突地区的战略扩张过度。 德国外交关系委员会(DGAP)主任托马斯·克莱恩-布罗克霍夫(Thomas Kleine-Brockhoff)向德国之声表示，特朗普领导下的美国现在正试图“建立一个大国霸权世界，与俄罗斯和中国一起建立一个全球理事会”，相当于由大国控制的势力范围。 结果，国际法和联合国等多边机构正在受到美国、中国和俄罗斯的破坏（每个机构都有自己的原因和意图）。 萨克瑟出版了一本同名书，他表示，结果是一个“狼世界”，意思是一个“强者法则战胜强者力量的世界……”

reflection.en: The shifting global landscape, where old norms are challenged, highlights the critical need for clear vision. Without a shared understanding of the path forward, societies can drift into uncertainty or chaos. Yet, with thoughtful leadership and a commitment to inclusive principles, these moments of disruption can indeed become opportunities to build a more...
reflection.zh: 全球格局变迁，旧有规范面临挑战，这凸显了清晰愿景的关键性。若缺乏对未来方向的共同理解，社会可能陷入不确定或混乱。然而，若有深思熟虑的领导和对包容原则的承诺，这些颠覆时刻确实能成为建立更公正、更稳定未来的机会。

title.en: 18 dead in Lebanon as Israel retaliates for soldier deaths, ignoring US-Iran deal
title.zh: 以色列为士兵死亡进行报复，黎巴嫩18人死亡，无视美伊协议

summary.en: Following the deaths of four IDF soldiers, Israel retaliated, resulting in 18 deaths in Lebanon. National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir issued a severe threat, stating, "Lebanon must burn."
summary.zh: 在四名以色列国防军士兵死亡后，以色列进行了报复，导致黎巴嫩18人死亡。国家安全部长伊塔马尔·本·格维尔发出了严厉威胁，称“黎巴嫩必须燃烧”。

body.en:
Fighting flared in Lebanon on Friday, with authorities reporting 18 killed in Israeli airstrikes across the south and Israel announcing the deaths of four of its soldiers.

The violence is the worst since the sealing of a US-Iran deal to halt the wider Middle East war, which was supposed to also pause the fighting between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon.

The deaths of the soldiers drew a furious reaction in Israel, with far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir saying "Lebanon must burn".

The Lebanese health ministry said the "intensive" strikes "resulted in a preliminary toll of 18 martyrs and 33 wounded" in at least 10 villages and towns.

"The IDF (military) struck more than 80 command centres, terrorists, launch positions, and additional terrorist infrastructure sites in the area of Nabatieh and additional areas in southern Lebanon," an army statement said.

"Furthermore, during the strikes, dozens of Hezbollah terrorists operating in the command centres were eliminated."

Iran-backed Hezbollah, meanwhile, said it was attacking Israeli forces around the southern town of Nabatieh.

Other Israeli strikes targeted the Baalbek region in the east of the country, which had been largely spared since the start of the conflict on 2 March.

Israel said its strikes in Baalbek and the Bekaa Valley were in response to "repeated violations of the ceasefire by Hezbollah", which it said "continues to prepare and carry out terrorist attacks against Israeli soldiers".

Earlier its military announced that Lieutenant Colonel Dor Gedalia Ben Simhon had "fallen in combat" along with three other soldiers whom it did not immediately identify.

A military official said the incident involved an impact from "a suspicious target" on an Israeli tank, with Israeli military correspondents reporting it had been hit by "a suspected drone or anti-tank missile".

In a separate statement the military also reported that a reserve officer was severely wounded "as a result of an explosive drone impact in southern Lebanon", with four other soldiers lightly injured.

"With all due respect to the Americans, Israel must make it clear to the entire world that the blood of our sons and the security of our citizens are not up for bargaining. All of Lebanon must burn," Ben Gvir said in a statement.

"For every tear shed by an Israeli mother, a thousand Lebanese mothers must weep," he added.

US officials including president Donald Trump have expressed frustration at Israel's campaign in Lebanon, which it has pursued in spite of US negotiations with Iran and a separate ceasefire agreed in April that was meant to halt the fighting...
body.zh: 周五，黎巴嫩爆发战斗，当局报告称，以色列对南部地区的空袭造成 18 人死亡，以色列还宣布 4 名士兵死亡。 这是自美伊签署协议以停止更广泛的中东战争以来最严重的暴力事件，该协议本应暂停以色列和黎巴嫩真主党之间的战斗。 士兵的死亡在以色列引起了强烈反应，极右翼的以色列国家安全部长伊塔马尔·本·格维尔表示“黎巴嫩必须燃烧”。 黎巴嫩卫生部表示，“密集”的袭击在至少 10 个村庄和城镇“初步造成 18 名烈士和 33 人受伤”。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 一份军方声明称：“以色列国防军袭击了纳巴蒂耶地区和黎巴嫩南部其他地区的 80 多个指挥中心、恐怖分子、发射阵地和其他恐怖分子基础设施。” “此外，在袭击期间，数十名在指挥中心活动的真主党恐怖分子被消灭。” 与此同时，伊朗支持的真主党表示，他们正在袭击南部城镇纳巴蒂耶周围的以色列军队。 以色列的其他袭击目标是该国东部的巴勒贝克地区，自 3 月 2 日冲突爆发以来，该地区基本上没有受到影响。 以色列表示，对巴勒贝克和贝卡谷地的袭击是对“真主党一再违反停火协议”的回应，并称真主党“继续准备和对以色列士兵发动恐怖袭击”。 早些时候，军方宣布多尔·吉达利亚·本·西蒙中校和其他三名士兵“在战斗中阵亡”，但军方没有立即透露这三名士兵的身份。 一名军方官员表示，这起事件涉及“可疑目标”对以色列坦克的撞击，以色列军事记者报道说，这辆坦克被“可疑的无人机或反坦克导弹”击中。 军方在另一份声明中还报告称，一名预备役军官“因黎巴嫩南部无人机爆炸撞击”而受重伤，另外四名士兵受轻伤。 本·格维尔在一份声明中表示：“尽管对美国人表示应有的尊重，但以色列必须向全世界表明，我们儿子的鲜血和我们公民的安全是不容讨价还价的。整个黎巴嫩都必须被烧毁。” 他补充说：“以色列母亲的每一滴眼泪，都必须让一千名黎巴嫩母亲哭泣。” 包括总统唐纳德·特朗普在内的美国官员对以色列在黎巴嫩的行动表示失望，尽管美国与伊朗进行了谈判，并且在四月份达成了旨在停止战斗的单独停火协议，但以色列仍在黎巴嫩继续进行行动......

reflection.en: The news of escalating violence and threats of further destruction highlights the destructive cycle of retaliation. In moments of profound loss and anger, it is challenging to resist the urge to respond with equal or greater force. Yet, Yahweh's word calls us to break this pattern, seeking to overcome evil not with more evil, but with good.
reflection.zh: 暴力升级和进一步破坏的威胁，凸显了报复的破坏性循环。在遭受深重损失和愤怒的时刻，抵制以同等或更大武力回应的冲动是极具挑战的。然而，雅伟的话语呼召我们打破这种模式，寻求不以恶报恶，而是以善胜恶。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: For women in China frustrated by sexism, female comics are offering a release
title.zh: 在中国，女性喜剧演员为厌倦性别歧视的女性提供宣泄出口

summary.en: Standup comedy in China is providing a platform for women to discuss sensitive topics, including sexism, offering a sense of release and shared experience. Performers, however, remain cautious of censorship limits as they navigate this space in venues like a small performing arts theatre in east Beijing.
summary.zh: 中国的脱口秀喜剧为女性提供了一个平台，让她们可以讨论包括性别歧视在内的敏感话题，从而获得宣泄和共同的体验。然而，表演者们在北京东部一家小型表演艺术剧院等场所进行表演时，仍对审查限制保持警惕。

body.en: Standup comedy gives women a space to talk about certain topics that have become more sensitive, while performers remain wary of censorship limits Packed into the upstairs theatre of a small performing arts space in east Beijing, more than 100 people, mostly women, are giddy with anticipation. “Who did you come to see?” asks the MC, fashionably dressed in a faded denim two-piece suit. The answer is bellowed in unison back to him: “Fang Zhuren!” Fang Shaoli, AKA Director Fang ( Fang Zhuren ), has built a cult following in China in the past two years. Decidedly less fashionable than the evening’s host, Fang is dressed in a yellow hoodie and dark blue jeans. Her everywoman attire is part of the appeal. With a stout frame and short, sensible haircut, Fang, who was born in 1975, hails from rural part of east China’s Shandong province. Before discovering the art of standup comedy she worked in factories and on construction sites, but mainly lived as a housewife to a difficult husband. Her jokes riff on the deep sexism that permeates Chinese culture, particularly away from the big urban centres like Beijing and Shanghai. Continue reading...
body.zh: 单口喜剧为女性提供了谈论某些变得更加敏感的话题的空间，而表演者们仍然对审查制度的限制保持警惕北京东部一个小型表演艺术空间的楼上剧场里，有 100 多人（其中大部分是女性）满怀期待。 “你是来看谁的？”身穿褪色牛仔两件套西装的主持人问道。对方齐声喊道：“方主任！”方绍立，又名方主任（方主任），过去两年在中国建立了一批狂热的追随者。方穿着黄色连帽衫和深蓝色牛仔裤，明显不如当晚主持人时尚。她的普通女性着装是其吸引力的一部分。方出生于1975年，来自中国东部山东省的农村地区，身材魁梧，留着一头漂亮的短发。在发现单口喜剧艺术之前，她曾在工厂和建筑工地工作过，但主要是作为一位难相处的丈夫的家庭主妇生活。她的笑话反复提及了渗透在中国文化中的根深蒂固的性别歧视，尤其是在远离北京和上海等大城市中心的地方。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the human need to express frustrations and experiences, especially when facing societal pressures like sexism. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us of the importance of speaking up for those whose voices are often unheard, advocating for justice and dignity. Even in challenging environments, creative expression can offer a vital space for shared...
reflection.zh: 这个故事突显了人类表达挫折和经历的需求，尤其是在面对性别歧视等社会压力时。箴言31:8-9提醒我们，为那些常常被忽视的声音发声，倡导公义和尊严是何等重要。即使在充满挑战的环境中，创造性的表达也能为共同的理解和释放提供一个重要的空间，这反映了雅伟对边缘群体的关怀。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Border Force officer and Hong Kong trade official jailed for spying for China
title.zh: 英国边境部队官员和香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动被判入狱

summary.en: A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official have been sentenced to 10 and eight years in prison, respectively, after being convicted of spying for China. These are the first convictions under the UK's National Security Act.
summary.zh: 一名英国边境部队官员和一名香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，刑期分别为10年和8年。这是英国根据《国家安全法》首次定罪的案件。

body.en: Peter Wai and Bill Yuen sentenced to 10 and eight years at Old Bailey in first convictions under National Security Act A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official based in London have been jailed for spying for China in the first such conviction in British criminal history. Peter Wai, who conducted “shadow policing” operations on Chinese dissidents in the UK, was sentenced to 10 years, while his handler, Bill Yuen, received an eight-year term. Continue reading...
body.zh: Peter Wai和Bill Yuen根据《国家安全法》首次在老贝利被判刑10年和8年。一名英国边防部队官员和一名驻伦敦的香港贸易官员因为中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，这是英国犯罪史上的首次此类定罪。在英国对中国持不同政见者进行“影子警察”行动的韦彼得被判处10年徒刑，而他的经纪人袁比尔则被判处8年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the profound breach of trust when public officials betray their duties. Yahweh's word reminds us that faithfulness in small responsibilities reflects our character in larger ones. May we all strive for integrity in every role we are given, understanding that honesty builds trust and strengthens the fabric of society.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了公职人员背叛职责时对信任的严重破坏。雅伟的话语提醒我们，在小事上忠心的人，在大事上也忠心。愿我们都在所担任的每一个角色中追求正直，明白诚实能建立信任并巩固社会结构。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.en: Inspired by Ukraine, and worried by China: Taiwan teaches its citizens how to fly drones
title.zh: 受乌克兰启发，担忧中国大陆：台湾教导市民如何驾驶无人机

summary.en: Ordinary citizens in Taiwan are enrolling in drone piloting courses, inspired by events in Ukraine and concerned about a potential military threat from China. These courses teach participants, young and old, how to operate drones for various purposes.
summary.zh: 受乌克兰局势的启发并担忧中国大陆的军事威胁，台湾普通民众（包括年轻人和老年人）正在参加无人机驾驶课程。这些课程旨在教授学员如何操作无人机以应对潜在情况。

body.en: Ordinary Taiwanese, young and old, are joining courses to learn how to fly drones amid looming China military threat In a small, crowded room in Taipei, Pan Chien-chin is trying to keep a drone hovering steadily. Imagining himself flying a plane, he gently nudges controller joysticks to guide the insect-like device as it hums through the air. Cheers break out as Pan, who has never flown a drone before, steers it around a rectangular course marked by traffic cones without crashing. Around him are about two dozen fellow trainees, all signed up for the same course: Taiwan’s first civil defence drone training programme. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾普通民众，无论老少，都在参加课程，学习如何在迫在眉睫的中国军事威胁下驾驶无人机。在台北一间拥挤的小房间里，潘建钦正努力让无人机保持稳定盘旋。他想象自己驾驶一架飞机，轻轻推动控制器操纵杆，引导昆虫般的设备在空中嗡嗡作响。当潘以前从未驾驶过无人机时，他驾驶无人机绕着一个由交通锥标标记的矩形航线飞行，没有坠毁，引发了欢呼声。他周围大约有两打学员，他们都报名参加同一门课程：台湾首个民防无人机训练计划。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The story highlights a community's proactive response to perceived threats, reflecting a natural human inclination to prepare for potential dangers. Proverbs reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing trouble and taking steps to protect ourselves and our communities. Such foresight, when coupled with a reliance on Yahweh, can guide us in uncertain times.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻讲述了一个社区如何积极应对潜在威胁，反映了人类为可能出现的危险做准备的自然倾向。箴言提醒我们，预见祸患并采取措施保护自己和社区是智慧之举。这种远见，若能与对雅伟的信靠结合，便能在不确定的时期指引我们。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Lululemon apologises after Japanese drum row at Great Wall yoga event
title.zh: Lululemon因长城瑜伽活动中的日本太鼓风波致歉

summary.en: The activewear brand Lululemon issued an apology after an online uproar in China. The controversy stemmed from a promotional yoga event held on the Great Wall of China, where a Japanese taiko drum was mistakenly featured instead of a Chinese drum, despite the event being intended to celebrate Chinese culture.
summary.zh: 运动服饰品牌Lululemon因在中国长城举办的瑜伽推广活动中误用日本太鼓而引发网络争议后，发表了道歉声明。尽管该活动旨在庆祝中国文化，但这一失误在中国引发了线上轩然大波。

body.en: Online uproar follows Canadian brand’s use of taiko drum at sponsored festival held to celebrate Chinese culture The activewear brand Lululemon has apologised after a promotional event held on the Great Wall of China appeared to mistakenly feature a Japanese drum, prompting an uproar. The Canadian-headquartered company, known for its upmarket leggings, has been growing rapidly in China and arranged for a yoga festival to take place in late May on a section of the wall near Beijing. Continue reading...
body.zh: 加拿大品牌在为庆祝中国文化而举办的赞助节日上使用太鼓，在中国引起网络轩然大波运动服品牌 Lululemon 在中国长城举行的一次促销活动中错误地使用了日本太鼓，引发轩然大波，该品牌已道歉。这家总部位于加拿大的公司以其高档瑜伽紧身裤而闻名，在中国发展迅速，并于五月底在北京附近的一段长城举办了一场瑜伽节。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This incident reminds us how quickly a seemingly small cultural misstep can ignite widespread public sentiment, especially in the digital age. Just as a tiny spark can set a vast forest ablaze, unintentional actions or symbols can inadvertently cause significant uproar and division. It underscores the need for careful consideration and humility in our...
reflection.zh: 这起事件提醒我们，一个看似微小的文化失误，尤其在数字时代，能多么迅速地引发广泛的公众情绪。正如一点火花能点燃整片森林，无意的行为或象征也可能不经意间造成巨大的争议和分歧。这强调了我们在互动中需要谨慎思考和谦卑，认识到即使是微小的细节也可能产生深远的影响。

verse.textEn: The tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.
verse.textZh: 舌头在百体里也是最小的，却能说大话。看哪，最小的火能点着最大的树林。

title.en: They were forced into marriage and abused. Now women facing exploitation in China have a glimmer of hope
title.zh: 她们被迫结婚并遭受虐待。现在，中国面临剥削的女性有了一线希望

summary.en: Female activists are secretly working to locate and assist vulnerable women in China who have been forced into marriage and subjected to abuse, as they believe authorities are not adequately protecting them.
summary.zh: 在中国，女性活动家们正在秘密寻找并帮助那些被迫结婚并遭受虐待的弱势女性，因为她们担心官方未能提供足够的保护。

body.en: Female activists are working in the shadows to find and support vulnerable women they fear are being failed by authorities Last summer, Xiaocao, a softly spoken woman in her 40s, received a tip-off that in Lüliang, a small city in China’s Shanxi province, vulnerable women were being forced into marriages. Along with another volunteer, she wanted to investigate. After leaving Beijing, the two volunteers travelled south for hours, on trains and in rental cars. A few villages turned out to be dead ends. But on the final day of their trip, the women stopped in a county where they’d heard about a woman with learning disabilities who was “married” to two brothers. Soon, they found her. Continue reading...
body.zh: 女性活动人士正在暗中寻找和支持她们担心当局辜负的弱势女性。去年夏天，40 多岁、说话轻声细语的小曹接到举报，称在中国山西省的一个小城市吕梁，弱势女性正在被迫结婚。她想和另一名志愿者一起进行调查。离开北京后，两名志愿者乘坐火车和租车向南行驶了几个小时。一些村庄变成了死胡同。但在旅行的最后一天，妇女们在一个县停下来，她们听说那里有一名有学习障碍的妇女“嫁给”了两个兄弟。很快，他们就找到了她。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the courageous work of activists who step in when vulnerable individuals are failed by systems meant to protect them. Their efforts embody the call to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, advocating for justice and dignity for the exploited.
reflection.zh: 这个故事彰显了活动家们的勇气，当弱势群体未能得到应有的保护时，她们挺身而出。她们的努力体现了为那些无法为自己发声的人说话的呼召，为受剥削者争取正义和尊严。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: The Guardian view on the global baby bust: people are having fewer children – even where they say they want more | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》观点：全球生育率暴跌——人们生育的孩子越来越少，即使他们说想要更多 | 社论

summary.en: A new report indicates that global fertility rates are falling faster and spreading further than anticipated, with India's fertility now below the level needed for population stability. This trend means that two-thirds of the world's population now lives in countries with declining birth rates.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，全球生育率下降的速度和范围都超出了预期，印度生育率已降至维持人口稳定所需的水平以下。这一趋势意味着全球三分之二的人口生活在生育率下降的国家。

body.en: Indian fertility has fallen below the rate required for population stability, in further evidence of the unexpectedly rapid decline in births internationally The global fall in fertility rates has arrived faster and spread further than anticipated. Two-thirds of people now live in countries that have slipped below the replacement rate – 2.1 births per woman – required for a stable population. Last month, India revealed that its fertility rate had fallen to just 1.9 . The world’s two most populous nations, which pursued cruel and coercive policies to cut births, both face shrinking populations. China’s fertility rate is now around 1, and births last year fell below 8 million – just over half the number projected when the “one child” policy was axed 10 years ago, and comparable to the total in 1738, when its population was 150 million. It’s further proof that what was seen as a phenomenon of rich nations has spread far beyond them. East Asia led the way. But Albania and Chile have far lower rates than the US or England and Wales (themselves experiencing record lows of 1.6 and 1.4). Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? body.zh: 印度的生育率已降至人口稳定所需的水平以下，这进一步证明了国际上出生率出人意料地迅速下降。全球生育率下降的速度和蔓延范围都超出了预期。目前，三分之二的人口生活在人口更替率（每名妇女生育 2.1 胎）以下的国家。上个月，印度透露其生育率已降至仅 1.9。世界上两个人口最多的国家都推行残酷和强制性的政策来减少生育，但都面临着人口萎缩的问题。目前中国的生育率约为1，去年的出生人数跌至800万以下——仅略高于10年前取消“独生子女”政策时预计数字的一半，与1738年的总人口相当，当时的人口为1.5亿。这进一步证明，被视为富裕国家现象的现象已经远远超出了它们的范围。东亚处于领先地位。但阿尔巴尼亚和智利的利率远低于美国或英格兰和威尔士（它们自己也经历过 1.6 和 1.4 的历史低点）。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

title.en: US military plans major war stockpile on Australian soil
title.zh: 美国军方计划在澳大利亚建立大型战争储备

summary.en: The United States military is planning a significant accumulation of weapons on Australian territory. This move is described as a key part of an Asia-wide regional defense strategy aimed at countering the growing influence of China.
summary.zh: 美国军方正计划在澳大利亚领土上大量储备武器。此举被描述为一项旨在对抗中国崛起势力的亚洲区域防御战略的关键组成部分。

body.en:
The US military is planning a permanent war-ready weapons stockpile for its marine corps on Australia's southeast coast beyond the range of most Chinese missiles, tender documents show and officials confirmed to the Agence France-Presse news agency (AFP).

The development of the stockpile, a first for the US marine corps in Australia, comes as the United States is keen to leverage the continent's strategic location in the South Pacific to counter China's rapid military build-up, analysts said.

The US marine corps began global prepositioning of military supplies during the Cold War — using floating stores on ships and caves in Norway where weapons, ammunition and vehicles to sustain thousands of troops are kept.

The first land stockpile in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to open this year in the Philippines, close to potential flashpoints in the South China Sea.

Documents published by the US navy this month show advanced planning for an even larger Australian stockpile, with US$30 million ($42.4M) allocated to build warehouses and offices in southeastern Victoria state for "critical forward provisioning".

The Australian stockpile, expected to reach full capacity by 2028, will be kept in Melbourne before being moved to US warehouses to be constructed next year at an Australian military base at Bandiana in rural Victoria, tender documents show.

Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, a sensitive issue in a country that has a security alliance with the United States and is hosting an increasing variety of US forces on rotation at Australian defence bases.

The US navy is engaging a global defence contractor to employ around 110 engineers, mechanics, material and safety specialists to manage the Australian stockpile, which includes "crew-served weapons", the documents show.

"Marine corps activities in Australia support integrated global sustainment by maintaining ready-for-issue equipment and supplies for operations and exercises across the Indo-Pacific," a US marine corps forces pacific spokesperson told AFP.

The spokesperson declined to comment on contract details or force planning assumptions but said marines' equipment is kept at "high readiness".

Contracting arrangements and the operation of the facility would be made in close coordination with Australia's Department of Defence.

"These activities improve responsiveness, strengthen interoperability with allies and partners, and support a range of missions across the Indo-Pacific," the spokesperson said, using an alternative description for the Asia-Pacific region.

title.en: Charging ahead: EVs outpace growth predictions
title.zh: 电动汽车：超越增长预期，加速前进

summary.en: Electric vehicles are becoming more affordable, efficient, and capable of longer distances, exceeding initial growth forecasts. China is leading this transition, with Europe and other nations rapidly advancing as well.
summary.zh: 电动汽车正变得更便宜、更高效，续航里程也比以往任何时候都长，其增长速度超出了预期。中国正在推动这一转型，而欧洲和其他国家也正在迅速追赶。

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

title.en: Girlfriends review – love and growing pains in queer coming-of-age tale that goes from Hong Kong to Taiwan
title.zh: 女朋友》影评：一部从香港到台湾的酷儿成长故事，充满爱与成长的烦恼

summary.en: The film "Girlfriends" is a romantic drama by Tracy Choi, following one woman's journey from high school to her mid-30s, exploring love and the challenges of growing up within a queer coming-of-age narrative set between Hong Kong and Taiwan.
summary.zh: 电影《女朋友》是崔允信执导的一部浪漫剧情片，讲述了一名女性从高中到三十多岁的人生旅程，探讨了在香港和台湾之间发生的酷儿成长故事中的爱与成长烦恼。

body.en: A trio of actors play one woman from high school to her mid-30s in Tracy Choi’s thoughtful romantic drama It can stretch credibility a little when an actor plays the same character over a long time span in one film. Richard Linklater solved the problem in Boyhood by shooting scenes over succeeding years; AI and de-ageing effects are now an option. With this intimate queer coming-of-age drama, film-maker Tracy Choi instead casts a trio of actors to play one woman from high school to her mid-30s. The three don’t look particularly alike; their temperaments overlap but are by no means identical. The point is perhaps to show how intense the transitions into adulthood are, how unrecognisable are the people we used to be. Working backwards, Girlfriends begins in Hong Kong, where 34-year-old film director Lok (Fish Liew) lives with her actor girlfriend Bei (Jennifer Yu). Five years earlier, Choi released a feature film, but her career has stalled. She is directionless and restless. Bei is also applying pressure to buy a flat and have a baby. The film then rewinds 12 years, to Taiwan, when Lok was a student with spiky orange hair, known as Choi (played by Elizabeth Tang). Some of the best scenes in the film come when her parents visit from Macau; Choi and her girlfriend Qing (Han Ning) have been pretending to be flatmates. Then, as the four of them eat dinner one night, unwilling to keep up the charade, Choi grabs Qing’s hand fiercely over the dinner table. She is coming out to her parents; they understand but say nothing. Another film might give us a big showdown, but this is probably how it would have happened in real life. Continue reading...
body.zh: 在 Tracy Choi 这部深思熟虑的浪漫剧中，三位演员扮演一名从高中到 30 多岁的女性。当一个演员在一部电影中长时间扮演同一个角色时，可信度会有所提高。理查德·林克莱特在《少年时代》中通过连续几年拍摄场景解决了这个问题。人工智能和抗衰老效果现在是一种选择。在这部亲密的酷儿成长剧中，电影制片人崔西·崔 (Tracy Choi) 聘请了三名演员来扮演一名从高中到 30 多岁的女性。这三个人看起来并不是特别相似。他们的性格有重叠，但绝不相同。重点也许是为了表明向成年的转变是多么激烈，我们过去的样子是多么难以辨认。时光倒流，《女朋友》的故事发生在香港，34 岁的电影导演乐（刘静茹饰）和她的演员女友贝（余珍妮饰）住在一起。五年前，崔发布了一部故事片，但她的事业却陷入了停滞。她没有方向，焦躁不安。贝还施加压力，要求买一套公寓并生孩子。影片随后将时间倒回12年前的台湾，当时乐还是一名留着尖尖橙色头发的学生，名叫崔（伊丽莎白·唐饰）。影片中一些最精彩的场景出现在她的父母从澳门来访时；崔和女友青（韩宁饰）一直假装是室友。然后，有一天晚上，当他们四个人吃晚饭时，崔不愿继续玩这个游戏，在餐桌上猛烈地抓住了庆的手。她向父母出柜了；他们明白但什么也没说。另一部电影可能会给我们带来一场大对决，但这可能就是现实生活中发生的情况。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This film explores the complex journey of self-discovery and relationships, highlighting the universal human experience of love and growing pains. In every person's unique path of identity and connection, we are reminded of the profound truth that each individual is created in the image of God, possessing inherent dignity and worth.
reflection.zh: 这部电影探讨了自我发现和关系的复杂旅程，突显了爱与成长烦恼的普世人性体验。在每个人独特的身份和联结之路上，我们都被提醒着一个深刻的真理：每个人都是按照雅伟的形象被创造的，拥有固有的尊严和价值。

title.en: Police 'dissapointed' following football fan chaos at watch events
title.zh: 球迷在观看赛事时发生混乱，警方对此感到“失望”

summary.en: Arrests were made at fan sites in both Sydney and Melbourne on Friday morning.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Victorian police have said that flares and fireworks were "disappointingly" set off by football fans gathered at Federation Square for the Australia-United States match on Saturday morning.

Arrests were made at fan sites in the Victorian capital as well as Sydney's Tumbalong Park, where thousands of Socceroos fans packed in to watch the event in the early hours.

One man was treated at the scene in Sydney for facial burns after being hit in the face by a flare.

In Melbourne, mounted police were forced to intervene after fans attempted to breach barriers at Fed Square when the popular site reached capacity just after 4am on Saturday.

About 7,500 fans packed the site in cold and rainy conditions, with 14 flares and one firework set off before the match, leading to two arrests.

The pair will be charged on summons, with police reviewing CCTV to identify those responsible for setting off the remaining flares.

"Enforcing prohibited items such as flares from entering the live site remains the responsibility of the venue," a Victoria Police spokeswoman said.

While fans celebrated the atmosphere, there was disappointment as the Socceroos' campaign suffered a setback with a 2-0 loss to the American team.

Former Socceroo Craig Foster, who was the MC at the live site, urged fans to stop letting off flares.

A 16-year-old boy was also arrested in relation to an alleged sexual assault of a woman about 4.55am.

Almost 9000 eager fans were redirected to AAMI Park, where the match was also livestreamed.

Sydney experienced similarly fiery scenes with two men, aged 20, arrested at Tumbarong Park in the city centre and later charged with possessing a bright light distress signal in a public place.

They were granted bail and are due to appear in court on Wednesday and police say investigations are still ongoing.

Conditions were more relaxed at Brisbane's South Bank, where thousands of fans watched the blockbuster clash, while excited crowds also gathered in Hobart, Canberra, and Perth.

body.en:
For years, as cases of the deadly H5 strain of bird influenza wreaked havoc among animal populations across the globe, Australia had been the sole continent to avoid it successfully — until now. The first positive case of the virus on the Australian mainland was confirmed on Saturday.

In a Canberra press conference, federal agriculture minister Julie Collins has confirmed H5 bird flu was detected in a migratory bird found in Western Australia.

A single migratory wild seabird potentially infected with the disease was found in Western Australia on June 14.

Before the suspected positive case was confirmed, Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said on Friday it would be "not unexpected".

"This will be sobering, but not unexpected given the spread globally," Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said.

The bird was a sub-Antarctic species — a brown skua bird. It was found on a remote beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park near Esperance, about 700km southeast of Perth.

WA Agriculture and Food Minister Jackie Jarvis said the bird was isolated after it was located in an unwell state on Sunday and died that night.

"I'm told it is not normal for them to be on the south coast of Western Australia," Jarvis said.

"But I am also told it's not uncommon if a bird is sick to actually be sort of blown off course, as it were."

Commonly known as bird flu, avian influenza is a contagious virus that predominantly affects bird species and can infect other animal populations, including humans.

The highly pathogenic H5N1 strain of avian influenza was discovered more than 20 years ago. Bird flu strains are classed in seriousness on a scale of pathogenicity — the capacity of the strain to cause the disease.

In birds, including poultry, seabirds and dense wild-bird colonies, H5 viruses can spread rapidly and cause severe disease, neurological defects and sudden death. Infected birds spread the virus through respiratory secretions and faeces, contaminating water, soil, feathers, carcasses and shared environments.

Australia has had previous outbreaks of avian influenza in poultry, but historically these have involved other strains, particularly H7 viruses, rather than the globally dominant H5N1 lineage.

The country’s first reported human H5N1 case in 2024 was travel-associated, in a child who likely acquired the infection overseas and later recovered.

The USA's dominant display proved too much for the Socceroos in Seattle with Australia going down 2-0, but still with a solid chance to progress to the next round of the FIFA World Cup.

The Socceroos defence that held so well against Türkiye had cracks in it, as the visitors conceded both goals in the first half. The second half was a more promising display from the Socceroos with young star Nestory Irankunde coming on and helping to lift the tempo, but not enough for a goal.

Socceroos coach Tony Popovic once again chose the element of surprise for his opening lineup and some Socceroos supporters were left scratching their heads with the two goal scorers against Türkiye, Nestory Irankunda and Conor Metcalfe, starting on the bench.

Mathew Leckie, known for his heroic goal against Denmark at the 2022 World Cup, and Nishan Velupillay started in their place.

Folarin Balogun ran down the left flank, and makes a cross into the six yard box where Australian defender Cam Burgess knocked it into the back of the net.

Jordy Bos received a yellow card after a block on Weston McKennie that pushed his face early in the second half and Alessandro Circati picked up another in the 31st minute.

In the 44th minute the USA went 2-0 up after a goal that Australian fans were hoping wouldn't stand.

They won a free kick on the edge of the penalty area. It was passed to the centre, with the shot coming from Sergiño Dest. The initial shot deflected by an Australian defender, going high, before being headed in by Alex Freeman.

Both goals were unlucky — an own goal and offside goal overturned by VAR — but the USA created far more chances.

At half time, Harry Kewell, part of SBS's presenter line-up, said the Socceroos have been "not good enough".

"We're just getting the ball and kicking it long where Toure has had no chance."

Popovic didn't waste any time in the break substituting Jason Geria, Conor Metcalfe and Nestory Irankunda on as Nishan Velupillay, Cam Burgess and Mo Touré went off.

But former Socceroo and broadcasting legend Craig Foster told SBS the decision not to start Irankunda had a high cost.

"I'm not sure why, Popa kept Irankunda on the bench, given that he was so brilliant in the first game. And the importance of the game against Turkiye was we went one-nil up instead of one-nil down.

"That's critical when you have a defensive style of play. So, you know, I think that decision has probably cost him. He's come on now in the second half to try and chase the game again. That's the most difficult position to be in."

body.en:
Petrol prices are at their lowest since mid-February, we've been told we may be over-estimating how much superannuation we actually need, and the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) held off on lifting interest rates this week.

That may sound like relief. But for households, there are still reasons to be cautious.

The national average for a litre of unleaded fell 5.6 cents last week to just over $1.69, according to the Australian Institute of Petroleum.

That's the lowest since mid-February, which was before the outbreak of the war in the Middle East.

It comes as the global oil price tumbled around 10 per cent this week following the unveiling of a framework to end the conflict — though negotiations are off to a shaky start .

While there are some ongoing uncertainties, the fall in oil prices should make petrol even cheaper in the coming weeks.

At the same time, the government's temporary fuel excise discount is scheduled to end , putting 26.3 cents per litre back onto the price of petrol and eating into any recent benefits.

The RBA left the cash rate unchanged at 4.35 per cent this week, delivering no immediate relief for mortgage holders.

While the decision was widely expected, the central bank's message remained cautious. Policymakers said inflation remains persistent and indicated further rate rises remain possible if price pressures do not ease as expected.

But with the economy slowing, three of the big four banks say the RBA may be done hiking interest rates, with cuts pencilled in for sometime in 2027.

We'll know more about the direction of inflation when the Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes the monthly consumer price index on Wednesday.

Many Australians may be overestimating how much they need to save for retirement.

New figures from the Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia (ASFA) show a single person retiring today needs around $630,000 in superannuation savings to fund a comfortable retirement. For a couple, that figure rises to around $730,000.

That includes top-level private health insurance, home internet, car ownership, regular meals out, annual domestic travel and an overseas trip every seven years.

body.en:
Ben Doherty in Apollo Bay Fri 19 Jun 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 19 Jun 2026 22.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google They came in the chill of winter to hear their speaker, a man known to most only as a name.

“Thank you,” Mohammad Ibrahim told the people of Apollo Bay. “Today I am proud to call Australia my home.”

Here, assembled before him in the Mechanics Hall, was the town that made that happen. A town that raised money so he could eat and his children could be clothed, raised hell with members of parliament, ministers, bureaucrats, journalists – anyone who would listen, and many who wouldn’t – to see that Australia upheld its obligation to him.

“Never underestimate the power of kindness,” he said. “Because what may seem like a small action to you can become the difference between hope and despair for someone else.”

During this country’s longest war in Afghanistan, Mohammad Ibrahim worked on Australia’s behalf , as an interpreter for a government-sponsored aid project in Uruzgan province.

The program built and ran schools for children in one of Afghanistan’s poorest provinces, it taught girls to read in places where few ever set foot in a classroom.

It vaccinated children who’d never visited a hospital, and trained midwives and doctors in a country with one of the highest infant mortality rates in the world.

Ibrahim was proud of the difference his work was making: “Working on those projects was an honour for me to serve my country and also help the Australian government.”

But when Afghanistan fell with terrifying swiftness to the Taliban in August 2021, Ibrahim was abandoned.

Like thousands who had believed in the mission of Republican Afghanistan, who’d trusted the promises of peace and prosperity, who’d been repeatedly assured by the countries they served they would be protected in the event of calamity, he and his family were forsaken.

International hopes for a reformed Taliban, that their desire for international legitimacy would restrain their most grotesque excesses – their brutality towards women, their violent persecution of minorities – were short-lived. The Taliban were unreformed.

In their eyes, Ibrahim was an “infidel” – a member of the Hazara ethnic and religious minority, and one who’d served the western invaders. With his young family, he was forced to flee into the mountains.

Over four long years in hiding , the family lived in caves in the highlands of Bamyan, walked over precipitous mountains to remote villages where the Taliban’s reach was limited. They also rented tiny rooms in Kabul, too afraid to go out, even to buy food, uncertain that the anonymity of the capital would be any protection.

Sometimes they had a few weeks in the same place, once a couple of months. Some days they were forced to move...

title.en: Which parties want to cut migration, and how far would they go?
